sections.heading: Enterprise *agentic AI services* and GenAI
sections.body:
Build assistants that answer from authorised enterprise information, and task-focused agents that use approved tools to complete work. We connect retrieval, enterprise integrations, evaluation and human approval around a defined business process.

An assistant helps a person find or interpret information; an agent can take an approved action. Bounded autonomy means agreeing the tools, permissions, approval points and escalation conditions before that action is available.

Still deciding which use case deserves investment? Explore [AI strategy & governance](/services/data-ai/ai-strategy-governance), or return to [Data & AI](/services/data-ai).

sections.heading: Keep the task and its limits visible
sections.description: These patterns show trigger, boundary and output. They are not client deployments; agree a success measure for the actual sources, users and systems.

items.title: Knowledge assistant
items.description: A user question retrieves authorised sources and returns a cited answer for verification.
items.bullets:
Boundary — user permissions and source scope
Review — verify the answer against its citations
Measures to agree — grounded answer quality and time to find information

items.title: Document review
items.description: A document becomes extracted fields and a summary, then moves to human approval.
items.bullets:
Boundary — no unreviewed downstream decision
Review — reconcile output with the document
Measures to agree — extraction accuracy and document review time

items.title: Task agent
items.description: A request becomes an approved API action, followed by logged completion or escalation.
items.bullets:
Boundary — approved tools and action limits
Review — approval for sensitive actions
Measures to agree — correct task completion and task turnaround time

sections.heading: A practical route to production AI
sections.description: Select, ground, evaluate and operate a defined workflow. Agree permissions, release evidence and operating responsibilities at each gate.

items.title: Select the use case — task and acceptance criteria
items.description: Identify users, task, source systems and approved actions. Agree the success measure, human approval points and latency/cost budget; define what the system must not do.

items.title: Ground the experience — source and tool design
items.description: Review permissions, source currency and retrieval scope. Agree tool/API contracts and exception handling with application and integration engineering teams.

items.title: Evaluate before release — reviewed test evidence
items.description: Agree representative evaluation data and test answer quality, unsafe actions and failure scenarios. Scope specialist Cyber Security validation and assign the release approver before operational use.

items.title: Observe and improve — operating handover
items.description: Agree tracing, cost review, support boundaries and change approval. Name rollback and escalation owners; use reviewed feedback to decide what to change, then evaluate it again.

sections.heading: Define a useful and bounded first scope
sections.description: Use the first discussion to clarify scope, approvals and ownership. Explore our [engagement models](/company/our-approach#engagement-models) before agreeing the delivery route.

items.title: Should we start with an assistant or an agent?
items.description: Start with an assistant when the need is to find, summarise or interpret information for a person. Consider an agent when the task has approved tools, clear permissions, exception paths and a reviewable completion condition.

items.title: What must be ready before operational use?
items.description: Agree authorised sources, tool boundaries, a representative evaluation set, release criteria and an operating owner. Test quality and failure behaviour in the intended workflow; a convincing demo alone does not establish this readiness.

items.title: Do products or accelerators come with the service?
items.description: No universal inclusion is assumed. Choose a software route or reusable accelerator only after reviewing the use case, deployment needs, integrations and limits. Implementation and ongoing operation require separately agreed responsibilities.

items.title: How can we engage and scope the next step?
items.description: Time & Materials suits discovery and co-development; Fixed Price fits a defined build with acceptance criteria. Dedicated Team or Managed Service arrangements depend on agreed delivery or operational ownership. Outcome-Based commercials require measurable, evidenced outcomes. Bring the task, sources, systems and constraints; an NDA can be arranged where required.
